reviews.comment: a lot of reading, pop quizzes, need to be able to read and speak spanish. expected 300+ word count for essay portion on final exam. nice lady though!

reviews.comment: All of the work for this course is based around the textbook. You'll read a different story before coming to class each day and she'll present the background of the story before going through the same questions you had to answer in the homework. She often puts the wrong dates in the online system, so due dates are confusing. Sweet, but unorganized.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professora Quintana is a really great professor! She is a tough grader when it comes to presentations but she is fair, so make sure you know your verb tenses! She made herself available outside of class and really does a lot to support student success. By the end of the semester, we all became friends and she made her class a fun place

pressure participation and discussion is good for a classroom

reviews.comment: Professor Quintana is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had! You can tell she really cares about her students. She acknowledges the different speaking levels students are at, and grades pretty easily if she knows you're at least putting in effort. This class was an easy and pleasant experience.

Prof. Quintana is amazing! We used a website to do weekly homework, & the majority of our lectures consisted of material featured from the homework. We had 4 in class presentations & she graded pretty lenient. As long as you make an effort, she'll see that and give you an A. We even had a end of the semester party b/c we all got so close. Take her!

If you want to be so bored that you would rather do stat homework, go ahead. The literature she uses is at such a basic level that I read it all in my high school Spanish classes. She is very hard to get in touch with. I would strongly advise anyone who cares about actually improving their Spanish ability to avoid at all costs.

There are 4 main projects that you have to present in Spanish to the class, she is not an extremely difficult grader and she gives good feedback. I absolutely loved taking her and look for sections she teches. She really cares about her students. On the last day of class we had like a party because we all got close to each other.
I really enjoyed Maria! She was so fun and provided a space to learn and have great conversations in Spanish! We had a fiesta at the end of the semester and it was so much fun! Definitely recommend!

Dr. Quintana is my favorite professor at A&M. She cares so much about her students and she is ready to help if you need it. I had a small class with her (about 10 people) and she made it so fun, and by the end we all felt as close as a family. Be ready to do lots of group work and discussions. As long as you put in effort you will be fine.

Stacked w/400 level undergrad class Learned a lot and, as expected, there is a ton of reading and discussion There was an almost total lack of organization with the readings being changed or modified just a few days before our 1/week 3hr. class Unclear grading criteria for weekly reports Inappropriate to have grad students write reports on readings
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The hardest Spanish class I've taken but so worthwhile. There was a 500 page paper a week and a reading with questions assigned every class. Her criticism was constructive, she was super understanding, and the discussions were productive. If you put in the work you'll get an A and learn lots.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers
